# hwatu

> Visual verification browser for AI coding agents: daemon-based WebKitGTK, real rendering, ~13ms median window spawn, ~216ms full verify pass

hwatu is AI-first: the primary user is a coding agent verifying web
UIs in its inner loop. Agent-facing features include headless/background
windows, snapshot/click/type/console automation, file upload, full-page
screenshots, and safe CAPTCHA/anti-bot challenge hand-off via
`hwatu challenge` / `hwatu challenge --wait` for manual user
resolution. hwatu detects and waits for challenges; it does not provide
automatic CAPTCHA bypass, solver API integration, token injection, or
fingerprint stealth.

The human side serves the hand-off: `hwatu focus <id>` materializes an
agent's live headless session as a normal window in the user's tiling
WM, so a person can solve a challenge or inspect a page, then the
agent resumes the same session. As a standalone minimal browser for
tiling WMs it works, but that is intentionally not the focus.

- [Agents guide](https://github.com/hongnoul/hwatu/blob/main/docs/agents.md): automation protocol for coding agents (the primary doc)
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/hongnoul/hwatu/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md): measured spawn latency, verification-loop cost, memory
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/hongnoul/hwatu/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md): AI-first plan of record, non-goals
- [README](https://github.com/hongnoul/hwatu/blob/main/README.md): install and usage
